strings.name: Larry Ellison
strings.summary: Born in New York and raised in Chicago, Ellison entered the technology industry without completing college. In 1977 he co-founded the company that became Oracle with Bob Miner and Ed Oates. As its long-serving CEO he drove expansion in databases and enterprise software, becoming executive chairman and CTO in 2014. Oracle subsequently expanded cloud computing and AI infrastructure through work by the company and its partners.
strings.coverageNote: Selected milestones verifiable through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: He co-founded Oracle and promoted commercial applications of relational databases, influencing enterprise data management and cloud computing infrastructure.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: New York City, United States; raised in Chicago.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Attended the University of Illinois and the University of Chicago without earning a degree.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Enterprise database business
strings.highlights.h1.text: He co-founded and long led Oracle, making commercial relational databases a major foundation of its enterprise software business.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From software to cloud
strings.highlights.h2.text: Under his leadership Oracle expanded through its listing and acquisitions; as executive chairman and CTO he later participated in its cloud development.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Cancels share-sale plan
strings.timeline.t1.text: Oracle announced cancellation of his 10b5-1 sale plan and said no company shares had been sold under it.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Participates in Stargate announcement
strings.timeline.t2.text: He participated in the White House announcement of Stargate AI infrastructure; investment and construction commitments did not establish full completion.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Hands over CEO role
strings.timeline.t3.text: He ended his tenure as CEO, which began in 1977, and became executive chairman and CTO.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Oracle acquires Sun
strings.timeline.t4.text: The company completed its acquisition of Sun Microsystems, adding hardware operations and technologies including Java.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Oracle goes public
strings.timeline.t5.text: Oracle listed on NASDAQ under his leadership, opening access to capital markets for further enterprise software expansion.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Co-founds company
strings.timeline.t6.text: With Bob Miner and Ed Oates, he founded Software Development Laboratories, which later became Oracle.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Studies at University of Chicago
strings.timeline.t7.text: After attending the University of Illinois, he studied at the University of Chicago without completing a degree.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in New York
strings.timeline.t8.text: He was born in New York City, adopted by relatives as an infant and subsequently raised in Chicago.
